name: Emmaus

identification.note: Several ancient sites have been proposed for Emmaus, none confirmed; the distance Luke gives (about seven miles from Jerusalem) does not match any single site with certainty.

related_people.name: Cleopas
related_people.role: one of two disciples who recognized the risen Jesus at table on the road here

unnamed_people.title: the unnamed companion of Cleopas
unnamed_people.role: walked with Cleopas to this village and recognized the risen Jesus in the breaking of bread

description: A village to which two disciples, including Cleopas, were walking on the day of the resurrection when the risen Jesus joined them unrecognized, opening the Scriptures until He was revealed in the breaking of bread (Luke 24:13-35).
family_friendly_summary: Emmaus was a village that two of Jesus's followers were walking to on the first Easter Sunday. The risen Jesus came alongside them, but they didn't recognize Him at first. He explained the Scriptures to them as they walked, and their eyes were opened when He broke bread with them at supper.
